<div id="hero" class="lead"> <p>I'm Yubo Jia, a Master's student in <strong>Hydrology &amp; Water Resources Engineering</strong> at Northwest A&amp;F University (NWAFU) in Yangling, Shaanxi. I also completed my B.Eng. at NWAFU. Originally from Yulin, Shaanxi, China, I expect to graduate in 2026 and plan to pursue a Ph.D. in <strong>Computer Science and Technology</strong> at Northwestern Polytechnical University (NPU) in Xi’an.</p>
<p>My research centers on the <span class="kw">AI–hydrology intersection</span>, especially <span class="kw">time-series modeling</span> for rainfall–runoff, <span class="kw">physics-guided deep learning</span>, and <span class="kw">uncertainty quantification</span> for decision-ready hydrologic forecasting and water resources management.</p> <ul class="hero-points" style="margin:.5rem 0 0 1rem; padding-left:.4rem;"> <li style="margin:.25rem 0;">Build generalizable sequence models that learn across many basins while retaining local behavior.</li> <li style="margin:.25rem 0;">Embed physical constraints and process cues into neural networks to improve robustness and interpretability.</li> <li style="margin:.25rem 0;">Deliver calibrated prediction intervals and risk-aware metrics to support operations.</li> </ul> <p style="margin-top:.5rem;">
  I value open science and reproducibility—notes and code are shared on GitHub, and I'm always glad to collaborate across
  <span class="kw-red">hydrology</span>, <span class="kw-red">computer science</span>, and
  <span class="kw-red">applied-statistics</span> communities.
</p> </div>
